That's fine. At least you didn't pretend to know.
column4: 그래요. 적어도 아는 척은 안 했으니까요.

column2: The bracelet goes back on her wrist. The clasp clicks shut.
column4: 그녀는 팔찌를 다시 손목에 차고 잠금장치를 딸깍 잠근다.

column2: First a sweet scent came through the door. Then the person.
column4: 문으로 달콤한 향기가 먼저 들어오고, 그다음 사람이 들어온다.

column2: Oh my, so this is the shop.
Way smaller than I thought.
Is Eleanor here?
Not here? Then my luck's good.
I was actually looking for her. Changed my mind as soon as I walked in.
column4: 사실 그 애를 찾으러 왔는데, 들어오자마자 마음이 바뀌었어요.

column2: Don't laugh. I just wanted to see what this place was like first.
column4: 웃지 마요. 먼저 어떤 곳인지 구경하고 싶었거든요.

column2: I asked around about you. Asked three people—two hadn't heard of you.
column4: 당신 이야기를 물어봤어요. 세 사람에게 물었더니 둘은 들어 본 적도 없대요.

column2: The other one said, "He doesn't cheat the scale."
column4: 나머지 한 사람은 저울을 속이지 않는다고 하더군요.

column2: All right, then I'll be a customer for once.
column4: 좋아요. 그럼 오늘은 저도 손님이 돼 볼게요.

column2: A slender bracelet lands on the counter, engraving inside facing up, edges bright.
column4: 가느다란 팔찌가 카운터에 놓인다. 안쪽의 각인이 위를 향하고 가장자리에서는 윤이 난다.

column2: Upper-tier work. I wore it twice.
column4: 상층에서 만든 거예요. 두 번밖에 안 찼어요.

column2: You decide the price.
...No, wait. You give the price first, then I'll decide whether to laugh.
column4: ……아니, 잠깐. 먼저 값을 불러 봐요. 웃을지 말지는 제가 정할게요.

column2: Seriously, though.
I found her a job. Upper-tier. Good pay, and it sounds good too.
column4: 그 애에게 일자리를 찾아줬어요. 상층에 있는 자리로요. 보수도 좋고 이름도 그럴듯하죠.

column2: One condition: she stops bringing up her mother's case in public.
column4: 조건은 하나예요. 사람들 앞에서 어머니 사건을 더는 입에 올리지 않는 것.

column2: She said no on the spot.
I tried to persuade her. She told me to drop it.
She'll come tell you herself.
column4: 그 애가 직접 와서 말할 거예요.

column2: Of course she'll come. She's here every day.
If she asks, say I came to sell something.
column4: 묻거든 물건 팔러 왔다고만 해 줘요.

column2: Don't make me sound better than I am.
column4: 저를 실제보다 좋은 사람처럼 이야기하진 말고요.

column2: She picks up her handbag, stops at the door, and glances back at the counter.
column4: 그녀는 핸드백을 들고 문 앞에서 멈춰 카운터를 돌아본다.

column2: I'll come again sometime. Even if I'm not selling anything.
column4: 언젠가 또 올게요. 팔 물건이 없어도요.

column2: The door closes. A sweet scent lingers by the counter.
column4: 문이 닫히고 달콤한 향기만 카운터 근처에 남는다.

column2: A young woman comes to the window, her bracelet tapping the counter edge.
column3: 一个姑娘来到窗口前，手腕上的镯子轻轻磕了一下柜沿。
column4: 젊은 여성이 창구에 다가오며 팔찌로 카운터 가장자리를 살짝 건드린다.

column2: Oh, this alley is even narrower than I thought.
column3: 哎呀，这巷子比我想的还窄。

column2: Walked all the way here, and my soles picked up three things. One I still don't want to identify.
column3: 我一路走过来，鞋底沾了三种东西，有一种我到现在都不想确认是什么。
column4: 여기까지 걸어오는 동안 신발 바닥에 세 가지가 묻었어요. 하나는 지금도 정체를 알고 싶지 않네요.

column2: Had to ask three people to find this place. They all said yours is the only pawnshop on this street that doesn't cheat people.
column3: 问了三个人才找到这儿，都说这条街上只有你一家当铺不坑人。
column4: 세 사람에게 물어서 겨우 찾았어요. 이 거리에서 손님을 속이지 않는 전당포는 여기 하나뿐이래요.

column2: So tell me—does that count as a compliment?
Yes.
You really don't talk much.
How many years have you been here?
column4: 여기서 장사한 지 몇 년 됐어요?

column2: A few.
A few. Just minding a room full of old things.
column3: 几年。就守着这一屋子旧东西。
column4: 몇 년. 낡은 물건이 가득한 방에서 계속 지내셨군요.

column2: ...I didn't mean it like that. I talk fast. Don't take it to heart.
column3: ……我不是那个意思。我嘴快，你别往心里去。
column4: ……그런 뜻으로 한 말은 아니에요. 제가 말이 빨라서요. 마음에 담아 두지 마세요.

column2: She sets her bag on the counter, digs out a bracelet, fingers still pressed on it.
column3: 她把包放在柜台上，从里面摸出一只镯子，指头还压在上面。
column4: 그녀는 가방을 카운터에 놓고 팔찌를 꺼낸다. 손가락은 여전히 그 위에 얹혀 있다.

column2: Old thing. Found it at home.
How much can I get?
Depends on the quality.
I don't know quality.
You decide. I won't haggle.
Really. Whatever you quote, I'll nod.
column3: 真的，你报多少我都点头。
column4: 정말이에요. 어떤 가격을 부르든 고개를 끄덕일게요.

column2: The bracelet is turned over. A thin line of engraving runs inside the band.
column3: 镯子被翻过来，内圈刻着一行极细的字。
column4: 팔찌를 뒤집자 안쪽 둘레에 가느다란 글씨가 새겨져 있다.

column2: Hey, don't worry about that.
...Fine. Sharp eyes.
If you're selling, I'll buy.
You're not going to ask where it came from?
You wouldn't tell me anyway.
Ha. Fair.
The bracelet goes into a wooden box under the counter. The lid snaps shut.
column3: 镯子进了柜台下的木盒，盖子扣上。
column4: 팔찌가 카운터 아래 나무 상자에 들어가고 뚜껑이 딸깍 닫힌다.

column2: You didn't try to cheat me on the price.
column3: 你报的价，倒没让我吃亏。

column2: I had a whole speech ready. Wasted.
column3: 我本来准备了一整套说辞，全废了。
column4: 할 말이 잔뜩 있었는데 다 쓸모없어졌어요.

column2: I figured if you pushed too hard, I'd know what to make of you.
column3: 我还想着，你要是压得太狠，我就知道该怎么看你。
column4: 값을 심하게 깎으면 어떤 사람인지 판단할 수 있을 거라고 생각했거든요.

column2: You didn't.
...So I guess I'll ask the real question.
Has a girl come by lately? Selling something?
column4: 요즘 물건을 팔러 오는 여자애가 있었나요?

column2: Upper-level accent, sharp tongue, about this tall, face longer than the shelves.
column4: 상층 말투에 성질이 날카롭고 키는 이 정도, 인상은 선반보다도 길게 찡그린 애요.

column2: Yes.
She actually came.
We grew up together. After what happened to her mother, my family's door might as well have said don't mention it.
column4: 우린 어릴 때부터 함께 자랐어요. 그 애 어머니에게 사건이 생긴 뒤 우리 집은 그 이야기를 꺼내지도 못하게 했죠.

column2: I called her. Told her to come stay at my place.
column4: 전화를 해서 우리 집에 와서 지내라고 했어요.

column2: She answered with two words: no need. Then hung up.
column4: 필요 없다는 두 마디만 하고 끊더군요.

column2: I was so mad I didn't sleep half the night. Next day I still texted her.
column4: 너무 화가 나서 밤을 반이나 설쳤어요. 다음 날에도 문자를 보냈지만요.

column2: She didn't answer a single one.
I'm not here to gossip.
I just want to know if she's been eating.
column4: 그 애가 밥은 먹고 지내는지 알고 싶을 뿐이에요.

column2: ...Don't laugh.
Fine. I talk too much. I know.
She slings the bag strap onto her shoulder and walks to the door.
column4: 그녀는 가방끈을 어깨에 걸고 문 쪽으로 걸어간다.

column2: Leave the bracelet with you for now.
I'll come redeem it in a few days.
Who am I looking for?
...You really don't dance around it.
A friend. Her mother had trouble, she got sent down, won't see anyone.
column3: 找一个朋友。她母亲出了事，她被赶下来，不肯见人。
column4: 친구요. 어머니에게 문제가 생겨 하층으로 쫓겨났는데 아무도 만나려 하지 않아요.

column2: Once I say that, you should know who.
column3: 我说到这儿，你该知道是谁了。

column2: She puts the bracelet back in her bag and fastens it.
column3: 她把镯子收回包里，扣好。
column4: 그녀는 팔찌를 가방에 도로 넣고 잠근다.

column2: You won't take it?
You didn't even check the quality before saying no.
column3: 你连成色都不看就说不要。

column2: Fine. I'll try somewhere else.
She puts the bracelet back in her bag. It takes her two tries to fasten the clasp.
column3: 她把镯子收回包里，扣子扣了两次才扣上。
column4: 그녀는 팔찌를 가방에 넣고 두 번 만에 잠금장치를 채운다.

column2: The bracelet is turned over. A thin line of engraving runs inside the band.
column3: 镯子被翻过来，内圈刻着一行极细的字。
column4: 팔찌를 뒤집자 안쪽 둘레에 가느다란 글씨가 새겨져 있다.

column2: Hey, don't worry about that.
...Fine. Sharp eyes.
If you're selling, I'll buy.
You're not going to ask where it came from?
You wouldn't tell me anyway.
Ha. Fair.
The bracelet goes into a wooden box under the counter. The lid snaps shut.
column3: 镯子进了柜台下的木盒，盖子扣上。
column4: 팔찌가 카운터 아래 나무 상자에 들어가고 뚜껑이 딸깍 닫힌다.

column2: You cut the price like it was nothing.
I thought you'd at least pretend to hesitate.
column3: 我本来想，你至少会装一下。
column4: 적어도 망설이는 척이라도 할 줄 알았어요.

column2: Fine. It's yours now.
...So I guess I'll ask the real question.
Has a girl come by lately? Selling something?
column3: 你这儿最近有没有一个女孩来卖东西？
column4: 요즘 물건을 팔러 오는 여자애가 있었나요?

column2: Upper-level accent, sharp tongue, about this tall, face longer than the shelves.
column3: 上层的口音，说话冲，个子这么高，脸拉得比货架还长。
column4: 상층 말투에 성질이 날카롭고 키는 이 정도, 인상은 선반보다도 길게 찡그린 애요.

column2: Yes.
She actually came.
